hero.lead: A nation of 10.9 million at the centre of Europe, with farmland across almost half its land and €8.67 billion of EU recovery and resilience funding.

capital.heading: Recovery funding, and every child a reader.

register.name: Flexi Bond for citizens, second subscription of 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · Dluhopis Republiky · issued 15 October 2026 · three-month savings bond, exchanged and reinvested unless the holder asks for payment · CZK 17.5bn of new deposits
register.note: A third subscription period is planned for 2026, starting around early December
register.text: A three-month government savings bond sold directly to citizens in the second subscription period of the Dluhopis Republiky in 2026; unless a holder asks for payment, it is exchanged and its yield reinvested for another three months. Flexi Bonds of CZK 44.6 billion were issued, with CZK 17.5 billion of new deposits; the bonds fund the state budget, from which the public services behind the seven standards are paid.
by: Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic

register.name: Government bond issuance programme, 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · Funding and Debt Management Strategy for 2026, second-half update, 17 July 2026 · total financing needs CZK 738.2bn, about 8.2% of GDP
register.note: Expected gross issuance of koruna government bonds on the domestic market in 2026; a new euro bond under Czech law remains possible
register.text: The Ministry of Finance expects to issue koruna government bonds of CZK 270 billion to CZK 370 billion on the domestic market in 2026, within total financing needs of CZK 738.2 billion, about 8.2% of GDP. Its strategy keeps open a new euro-denominated government bond under Czech law, sold at a Czech National Bank auction or by syndicate.
by: Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic

register.name: Government savings bonds for citizens (Dluhopis Republiky), spring 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued 15 July 2026 · fixed five-year CZK 37.9bn at a yield of 4.544% · inflation-linked five-year CZK 8.5bn · three-month Flexi Bond CZK 27.6bn at 3.75%
register.note: The highest value of government bonds sold in a single subscription period since direct sales to citizens began in 2011
register.text: Government bonds sold directly to citizens: nearly 92,000 people bought them, more than 69% of them for the first time. Orders reached CZK 80 billion, of which more than 92% was paid; the bonds fund the state budget, from which the public services behind the seven standards are paid.
by: Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic

register.name: Social government bonds, first issue
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · auction by the Czech National Bank 1 October 2025 · issued 3 October 2025 · CZK 7.0bn five-year at a yield of 3.914% · CZK 6.925bn ten-year at 4.448% · demand almost CZK 19bn
register.note: Proceeds allocated to 2024 state budget spending: CZK 11.284 billion on social inclusion and CZK 2.641 billion on education and vocational training
register.text: The Czech Republic’s first social bonds, issued under its Social Finance Framework of September 2025, priced about 15 and 10 basis points below comparable conventional government bonds. The allocation report of November 2025 assigns the net proceeds to eligible state budget spending of 2024, CZK 2.641 billion of it on education and vocational training, which serves the education standard.
by: Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Commission · grants €8.41bn, loans €0.26bn (amended, Council document of 20 July 2026) · eighth instalment 3 August 2026
register.note: Loans reduced in 2026 from €343.1 million to €260.2 million; the plan modified in 2024 stood at €9.2 billion
register.text: EU support for Czechia’s reforms and investments under the Recovery and Resilience Facility: €8,409,179,142 in grants and €260,167,635 in loans, paid in instalments against agreed milestones and targets, with 43% of the funds for climate objectives. The eighth instalment was paid on 3 August 2026.

register.name: North Bohemian water infrastructure (Severočeská vodárenská společnost)
register.detail: EIB · Just Transition Mechanism, Public Sector Loan Facility · signed 16 June 2026 · announced 14 July 2026 · with a €14M EU grant · total budget about €77M
register.note: Safer drinking water for about 300,000 inhabitants of the Ústí nad Labem Region
register.text: An EIB loan, with a €14 million EU grant under the Public Sector Loan Facility of the Just Transition Mechanism, to the water company SVS to rebuild water and wastewater treatment plants, upgrade distribution networks, mains and reservoirs, and eliminate untreated sewer outfalls. It serves the water standard, and sanitation within the shelter standard, for about 300,000 inhabitants.

register.name: Modernisation Fund, disbursement of July 2026
register.detail: European Commission and EIB · announced 2 July 2026 · €2.5bn for 51 projects in 11 Member States · €23.2bn made available by the Fund since January 2021
register.note: Czechia’s share of the disbursement; its projects include the decarbonisation of heat production in district heating systems
register.text: Czechia’s share of a €2.5 billion disbursement from the Modernisation Fund, which invests revenues from the EU Emissions Trading System in cleaner energy systems. Czech projects include the decarbonisation of heat production in district heating systems; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Modernisation of public infrastructure (Komerční banka)
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · approved 30 January 2026 · programme loan · 20% earmarked for the Karlovy Vary, Ústí nad Labem and Moravian-Silesian regions · in progress
register.note: For small municipalities and Just Transition regions, especially lower-income communities and older people
register.text: A CEB programme loan to Komerční banka to finance the upgrade of municipal and regional infrastructure and public services, including healthcare establishments, with a focus on Just Transition regions under economic and social strain. It serves the health standard and the people of small municipalities, especially lower-income communities and older people.

register.name: Power grid reinforcement and digitalisation (ČEZ)
register.detail: EIB · 2025 · in the EIB Group’s 2025 figures for Czechia, 12 February 2026
register.note: To integrate up to 5.5 gigawatts of renewable energy
register.text: An EIB loan to the electricity supplier ČEZ for grid reinforcements and digitalisation, which will enable the integration of up to 5.5 GW of renewable energy. It serves the energy standard with cleaner power.

register.name: High-voltage lines (ČEPS)
register.detail: EIB · 2025 · in the EIB Group’s 2025 figures for Czechia, 12 February 2026
register.note: To refurbish and extend more than 500 km of high-voltage lines
register.text: An EIB loan to the transmission system operator ČEPS to refurbish and extend high-voltage lines. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: EIB loans to the Czech Republic, drawn in 2025
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · Government Debt Management Annual Report for 2025, 27 February 2026 · water management CZK 7.2bn in four tranches · transport infrastructure CZK 13.0bn · railway corridor CZK 3.0bn
register.note: No new tranche was drawn in the second or third quarter of 2026
register.text: Tranches of EIB loans drawn by the state in 2025: CZK 7.2 billion for water management projects, CZK 13.0 billion to co-finance transport infrastructure and CZK 3.0 billion to modernise eight sections of the railway corridor to the Polish border. The water management tranches serve the water standard.
by: Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic

register.name: Equipment finance for small businesses and mid-caps (SG Equipment Finance Czech Republic)
register.detail: EIB · signed 31 July 2026 · announced 24 September 2026 · matched by SGEF · at least 20% for climate and environmental investments
register.note: €300 million in all with SGEF’s match, mainly in Czechia and Slovakia; 88% projected for EU cohesion regions
register.text: An EIB loan to SG Equipment Finance Czech Republic, a Komerční banka subsidiary, matched by the company, to finance investments by small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps in modern equipment, technology and transport. It serves the livelihood standard through smaller businesses.

register.name: Guarantee for mid-cap lending (UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia)
register.detail: EIB · 17 March 2026 · Growth4MidCaps Lending Envelope · loans may be denominated in Czech koruna
register.note: Lets the bank offer up to €400 million in new loans to Czech and Slovak mid-caps
register.text: An EIB guarantee to the local subsidiary of UniCredit that lets the bank lend up to twice the amount, €400 million, to manufacturing and export-oriented mid-caps in Czechia and Slovakia, with longer maturities and larger loans. It serves the livelihood standard.
by: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia

register.name: Affordable rental housing in Prague (Česká spořitelna)
register.detail: EIB · project 20230895 · approved 26 March 2025 · signed 21 May 2025 · framework loan · total cost about €188M
register.note: More than 700 new homes let long term below market prices to key workers
register.text: An EIB framework loan to Česká spořitelna for its subsidiary Dostupné bydlení České spořitelny to build more than 700 homes in four districts of Prague, let long term below market prices to key workers such as nurses, teachers and public sector workers. The EIB describes it as the first project of its type in the country; it serves the shelter standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 15.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Včelka
items.text: A Czech company whose online reading programme, created by experts in reading and learning difficulties, trains children’s reading technique, comprehension and early writing, and now also English and Spanish. More than 350 schools across the country use it in regular teaching, through a paid school licence.

items.name: Czech Federation of Food Banks
items.text: A federation of food banks that rescues about 10,000 tonnes of food a year from retail chains and producers and passes it to more than 1,500 non-profit organisations and to its own 261 distribution points. In 2025 its network supported 430,000 people, with food valued at CZK 721 million.

items.name: Zachraň jídlo
items.text: An association whose Zachraň oběd service collects surplus warm lunches from company and school canteens and delivers them, through charities, to shelters, single mothers, seniors and people experiencing homelessness. By November 2024 it had saved more than 88,000 portions on 27 routes, and in 2025 it piloted the service in Prague schools.

items.name: Kuchařky bez domova (Jako doma)
items.text: A vegan catering social enterprise of the non-profit Jako doma that gives work to women who have experienced homelessness; more than eighty women without a home or in another difficult situation have worked with it. Catering is its main income, and a 2025 campaign funded wages and support for ten women after it lost a key grant.

items.name: Teamium
items.text: A social enterprise that runs Bistro Teamcaffe in Brno, which provides work for eight people. It was featured in March 2026 with the Centre for Social Entrepreneurship in Brno, which supports social enterprises with consulting, mentoring and business connections.
